\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

The paper gives a closed-form record-law and fixed-setting asymptotic analysis
for one constrained latched killed-leakage sampled-counter D-MAP(2) subfamily.
The visible
record identifies the unordered survival/rate coordinates, not hidden labels
or response-side thermodynamic parameters without external calibration.  The
two-state fibre theorem makes this ambiguity exact in the larger killed-reset
class: separated rates generate a closed continuum arc whose only triangular
members are the two physical rate orderings, while equal rates generate a
singleton fibre.  The diagonal statement is deliberately narrow: it is only
the pointwise projected
limit at the fixed \(z_0=1/2\) candidate with its printed population covariance
certificate, and it carries no confidence-procedure interpretation.

The theorem-by-theorem comparison in
\Cref{sec:theorem-led-comparison} separates recalled proof inputs from the
model-specific calculations proved here.

\section{Related Work and Mathematical Comparison}\label{sec:theorem-led-comparison}

The introduction gives the mathematical narrative comparison with the closest
renewal-binary, weak-memory, waiting-time, partial-observation, and detector
papers.  This final section gives a compact theorem-by-theorem comparison with
the direct D-MAP, MAP, and discrete phase-type literature, followed by the
closest detector-model comparator.  Extended comparator tables and the search
ledger are placed in the supplementary material.

\subsection{Detector dead-time comparator}\label{subsec:detector-dead-time-comparator-main}

In the nonparalyzable continuous dead-time model, an accepted event is followed
by a fixed or random inactive period and then by a live waiting time; this
structure produces renewal count statistics and motivates classical
dead-time corrections and detector checks
\cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
GronbergDanielssonSjolin2018Nonparalyzable,MeeksSiegel2008DeadTime}.
Krause--Walenta's continuous exponential-recovery model for free-running SPADs
allows detection efficiency to recover continuously after dead time and fits
parameters from inter-detection intervals \cite{KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.
Such a detector need not have \(T_1(\cdot,R)=0\): after a click, physical
recovery and further evolution can occur before the next externally chosen bin
boundary.  In contrast, the present model is a sampled discrete D-MAP with
stochastic recovery before a click and an explicit post-click latch until the
boundary.
Its Palm zero-run law is
\[
g_k=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1
=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-\Gamma(1-s)s^k}
       {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\]
with the continuous equal-rate limit understood.  The contribution relative to
the detector dead-time literature is therefore not a generic dead-time
correction.  It is an exact quotient inverse for the sampled killed-leakage
D-MAP visible law, together with the renewal product and retained-record
covariance route that are valid only under the boundary-reset convention in
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main,prop:model-fragility-boundary-reset-main}.

\subsection{Theorem-by-theorem comparison with DMAP, DPH, and MAP theory}

\paragraph{Theorem A (record law).}
Alfa--Neuts supply the general D-MAP construction
\cite{AlfaNeuts1995DMAP}, while M\'esz\'aros--Telek study canonical
representations for general discrete order-two MAPs and RAPs
\cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}.  Those representation results
do not assert that the present triangular, deterministically reset subfamily is
renewal.  The additional calculation here is restricted to that subfamily: it
derives the Palm gap law, increasing hazard, one-mode covariance, and exact
\(1\)-dependence criterion.  These are elementary model-specific consequences,
not a new general DMAP theorem.

\paragraph{Theorem B (three-inclusion quotient inverse).}
The closest prior result is the canonical-coordinate analysis of discrete
order-two MAP/RAP models by M\'esz\'aros--Telek
\cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}, together with canonical MAP2
and matrix-exponential representation work
\cite{BodrogHeindlHorvathTelek2008MAP2Canonical,
TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}.  That literature constructs sparse or canonical
representatives and moment-matching maps for broader representation classes.
Theorem~B neither replaces nor strengthens those canonical-form theorems.  Its
narrow additional statement is the direct rational identity
\[
\frac{r_2-r_0^2}{r_1-r_0^2}=p-b
\]
for the latched killed-reset image, which converts three visible binary
inclusion probabilities into \((p+s,ps)\) and hence the complete visible
renewal law.  The estimand is a law-determining quotient, not a labelled
minimal DMAP2 representative.  We do not claim that this identity is absent as
an implicit specialization of canonical DMAP2 coordinates; the contribution
is the explicit three-inclusion specialization and its stability bounds.

\paragraph{Theorems C and D (asymptotics).}
The regenerative CLT, separated-batch method, and multivariate delta method are
standard inputs \cite{Zamparo2022RenewalBinary,Janson2024RenewalCLT,
AsmussenGlynn2007,FlegalJones2010BatchMeansSpectral}.  The paper's additional
work is bookkeeping for complete retained cycles, the explicit stopped-prefix
bounds, and transport to the three-inclusion quotient.  The sorted-root and
log-rate CLTs are direct delta-method consequences and are not claimed as new
asymptotic theory.

\paragraph{Theorem E (projection example).}
Metric-projection limits at smooth inequality boundaries are standard
\cite{Shapiro1987MetricProjection,FangSeo2021ProjectionTests}.  Theorem~E is
therefore presented only as a pointwise worked projection at \(z_0=1/2\), with
a reproducible covariance nondegeneracy certificate.  It makes no inferential
or novelty claim beyond this specialization.

\paragraph{Complete-law checking and the Markov--Palm score.}
Distributional-distance consistency, serial-independence basis tests,
finite-range and Hilbert-space central limit theorems, and local Gaussian
shift calculus are standard inputs
\cite{RyabkoRyabko2010ErgodicInference,Ryabko2012StationaryTesting,
SkaugTjostheim1993SerialIndependence,DedeckerMerlevede2003HilbertCLT,
vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
\Cref{thm:complete-visible-law-specification-main} combines those inputs with
the sampled-counter word law and an explicit rank-one Markov-gap path.  The
model-specific extension in
\Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main} is the exact closed
interaction space obtained by adding $q(0,0)=0$ to double centring, its
$\mu^{-1}$-scaled efficient projection, and the exchange-boundary calibration
of a trace-weighted score.  It claims pointwise strict local power in every
nonzero interaction direction, but neither a new general independence test
nor a uniform infinite-dimensional minimax envelope.

The dimension-free comparison
$W_2^2/4\leq Z_2$ and the multivariate Stein regularity estimate are external
\cite{BolbotowskiBouchitte2026ZolotarevWasserstein,
Meckes2009MultivariateStein}.  The model-specific calculation in
\Cref{prop:helmert-growing-layer-sharp-main} applies them to independent sums
of retained overlapping-Helmert blocks.  It keeps the block factor
$d_J^{3/2}$ explicit, while avoiding the additional ambient factor and
Gaussian comparison-block moment required by CMU's Yurinskii probability
bound.  This yields the sharp local-null boundary; no new general coupling
inequality is claimed.

\paragraph{Fibre results.}
Minimal-realization uniqueness is classical, beginning with Kalman and used
directly for MAP reduction and moment matching by Telek--Horv\'ath
\cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}.  Accordingly,
\Cref{thm:nstate-killed-reset-identifiability-dichotomy-main} is explicitly a
recalled orbit-fibre reformulation.  The new two-state assertion is
\Cref{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}: for the physical triangular
kernel, the complete Markovian orbit intersection is an explicit closed arc
between the rate-swapped endpoints and collapses exactly on the exchange
diagonal.  General MAP2 nonidentifiability and weak-equivalence results are the
nearest representation-theoretic comparators
\cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability,
RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP}; the claim here is only this exact
killed-reset sampled-counter specialization.

The further new assertion is
\Cref{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}: the unrestricted
interior fibre contains a positivity-preserving similarity manifold of exact
dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For serial kernels, Cumani's canonical failure-time
forms, acyclic DPH estimation, and order-two/three discrete PH canonical forms
are direct predecessors
\cite{Cumani1982CanonicalFailure,BobbioEtAl2003AcyclicDPH,
PappTelek2013DiscretePHCanonical,MeszarosPappTelek2014Traffic}.
\Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main} is consequently
stated as a killed-reset orbit-intersection calculation: the pure serial fibre
is exactly the rate-multiset permutation class, with collisions handled by the
confluent recurrence.  It is not claimed as a new general acyclic-DPH
canonical-form theorem.  General phase-type nonuniqueness remains fully
consistent with O'Cinneide's invariant-polytope analysis
\cite{OCinneide1989PhaseTypeNonuniqueness,OCinneide1991InvariantPolytopes}.

The longer comparator tables and search ledger are moved to the supplementary
material.

Renewal binary laws and CLTs &

Finite-dimensional laws and Gaussian limits for renewal or approximately renewal binary/counting processes. &
The present estimand is the sampled-counter D-MAP parameter quotient.  The paper proves that the triangular killed-leakage D-MAP lies in the renewal-binary class and then inverts \((r_0,r_1,r_2)\) to \((p+s,ps)\). \\
\addlinespace
MAP/D-MAP representation and moment theory &
Neuts \cite{Neuts1979MAP}; Alfa--Neuts \cite{AlfaNeuts1995DMAP}; Lucantoni \cite{Lucantoni1991BMAP}; Asanjarani--Hautphenne--Nazarathy \cite{AsanjaraniHautphenneNazarathy2026StructuredMAPMoments}, \doiid{10.1016/j.peva.2026.102562}. &
Marked-arrival representation, queueing/moment properties, and structured MAP moment calculations. &
Those objects are representation-level or moment-level.  Here the estimand is the visible renewal quotient recoverable from three binary inclusion probabilities, not a labelled MAP realization or a general structured-MAP moment class. \\
\addlinespace
Dead-time and photon-counting detector models &
M\"uller \cite{Muller1973}, \doiid{10.1016/0029-554X(73)90773-8}; Cantor--Teich \cite{CantorTeich1975}, \doiid{10.1364/JOSA.65.000786}; Yu--Fessler \cite{YuFessler2000}; Sarbazi--Safari--Haas \cite{SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime}; Gr\"onberg--Danielsson--Sj\"olin \cite{GronbergDanielssonSjolin2018Nonparalyzable}; Meeks--Siegel \cite{MeeksSiegel2008DeadTime}; Hadfield \cite{Hadfield2009}; Eisaman et al. \cite{EisamanEtAl2011}; Straka et al. \cite{StrakaEtAl2020SPADCounting}, \doiid{10.1109/JLT.2020.2994654}; Kirchhoff et al. \cite{KirchhoffEtAl2025Deadtime}; Jorgensen--Johnson \cite{JorgensenJohnson2026DED}. &
Nonparalyzable/paralyzable dead-time corrections, finite-window photon-count distributions, SPAD recovery and afterpulsing models, count-rate moments, and dead-time-constrained estimation. &
Those models target corrected count distributions, rates, or detector-specific recovery phenomena.  This paper fixes a discrete killed-leakage boundary-reset kernel and proves the visible renewal law, Palm gap hazard, inclusion-coordinate quotient inverse, and retained-cycle covariance transport for that kernel. \\
\addlinespace
Nonidentifiability of hidden representations &
Ryd\'en \cite{Ryden1996Aggregated}; Ram\'irez-Cobo--Lillo--Wiper \cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability}; O'Cinneide \cite{OCinneide1989PhaseTypeNonuniqueness}. &
Nonuniqueness or weak equivalence of labelled aggregated-Markov, MAP, or phase-type representations. &
The present inverse deliberately avoids labelled hidden identifiability.  It identifies only \((p+s,ps)\), the unordered pair \(\{p,s\}\), and visible functionals unless an external branch label is supplied. \\
\addlinespace
Weak-memory and correlation diagnostics in physics &
Hartich--Godec \cite{HartichGodec2021EmergentMemory}; Vollmar et al. \cite{VollmarEtAl2024Memory}; Brandner \cite{Brandner2025WeakMemoryPRE}, \doiid{10.1103/PhysRevE.111.014137}; Meyer--Brandner \cite{MeyerBrandner2026WeakMemory}; Su\'arez et al. \cite{SuarezEtAl2021MSMCanCannot}; Sartore--Teichmann--Stock \cite{SartoreTeichmannStock2025MarkovType}; Zhao--Makarov--Godec \cite{ZhaoMakarovGodec2025MarkovStateHolography}; Loos--Godec \cite{LoosGodec2025NonMarkovianEffects}. &
Memory strength, Markov-state adequacy, correlation or path-observable fidelity, and non-Markovian response diagnostics. &
Those works diagnose or model memory from broader dynamical data.  Here the theorem object is an exact one-mode covariance tail
\(\gamma_n=\rho(a-\rho)\lambda_{\rm hid}^{\,n-1}\), a zero-hidden-mode
\(1\)-dependence criterion, and a quotient inverse for the binary click record. \\
\addlinespace
Transition and waiting-time thermodynamic inference &
Harunari--Dutta--Polettini--Rold\'an \cite{HarunariDuttaPolettiniRoldan2022VisibleTransitions}, \doiid{10.1103/PhysRevX.12.041026}; van der Meer--Ertel--Seifert \cite{VanDerMeerErtelSeifert2022TransitionWTD}, \doiid{10.1103/PhysRevX.12.031025}; van der Meer--Deg\"unther--Seifert \cite{VanDerMeerDeguntherSeifert2023Snippets}; Maier--Fritz--Seifert \cite{MaierFritzSeifert2026SemiMarkovLD}. &
Visible-transition counts, transition-based waiting-time distributions, snippet statistics, semi-Markov large deviations, and entropy-production inference. &
Their estimands are thermodynamic or path-level functionals under partial observation.  This paper's waiting-time object is the Palm zero-run gap law \(g_k\) and its hazard, used to recover the visible renewal law and symmetric sampled-counter quotient. \\
\addlinespace
Partial-observation reconstruction and faulty observations &
Bauer--Seifert--van der Meer \cite{BauerSeifertVanderMeer2025Stroboscopic}, \doiid{10.1088/1751-8121/adbc52}; Maier--Seifert--van der Meer \cite{MaierSeifertVanderMeer2025HiddenPaths}; Ertel--Seifert \cite{ErtelSeifert2024BlurredTransitions}; van der Meer--Saito \cite{VanDerMeerSaito2025FaultyCoarseGraining}; Fritz--Ertel--Seifert \cite{FritzErtelSeifert2025ImperfectObservations}; Maier--H\"asler--Seifert \cite{MaierHaslerSeifert2026Blackouts}. &
Generator reconstruction, hidden-path inference, blurred-transition estimators, faulty coarse graining, imperfect-observation corrections, and blackout compensation. &
Those procedures target generators, paths, or thermodynamic quantities under observation error.  The present record is an exact binary renewal output of a specified D-MAP; the inverse stops at the visible quotient and does not reconstruct a full hidden generator. \\
\addlinespace
Constrained hidden-state and coarse-graining inference &
Tancredi et al. \cite{TancrediEtAl2024ConstrainedHMM}, \doiid{10.1088/1367-2630/ad5def}; Hilder--Sharma \cite{HilderSharma2024CoarseGraining}, \doiid{10.1137/22M1473996}, \arxivid{2201.10256}; Schilling \cite{Schilling2022CoarseGrained}. &
Parametric hidden-state discovery, quantitative Markov-chain coarse graining, and physical coarse-grained modelling. &
Those estimands are hidden-state models or coarse-grained transition structures.  Here the model class is fixed in advance and the theorem transports retained-record inclusion estimates through the quotient map \(\Phi(\Rinc)=(p+s,ps)\). \\
\addlinespace
Boundary and projection inference &
Shapiro \cite{Shapiro1987MetricProjection}, \shapirodoi; Chernoff \cite{Chernoff1954LikelihoodRatio}; Geyer \cite{Geyer1994ConstrainedM}; Self--Liang \cite{SelfLiang1987NonstandardLRT}; Fang--Santos \cite{FangSantos2019DirectionalDifferentiability}; Andrews \cite{Andrews1999BoundaryEstimation,Andrews2001BoundaryTesting}; Cavaliere et al. \cite{CavaliereNielsenPedersenRahbek2022BoundaryBootstrap}; Fang--Seo \cite{FangSeo2021ProjectionTests}, \doiid{10.3982/ECTA17764}; Fang \cite{Fang2021UnifyingShape}; Chen--Fang \cite{ChenFang2019FirstOrderDegeneracy}; Wang--Ye--Chen \cite{WangYeChen2024NonconvexBoundary}; Li \cite{Li2025ProximalBootstrap}. &
General boundary, cone, shape-restriction, directionally differentiable, and constrained-bootstrap inference. &
The present diagonal theorem is a fixed-null specialization: the D-MAP exchange-diagonal branch certificate, local projection onto \(F=\{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2):\sigma_2\le\sigma_1^2/4\}\), and retained-record covariance route at \(z_0=1/2\). \\
\end{longtable}

\appendix

\phantomsection\label{app:literature-search-protocol-main}
\paragraph{Supplementary protocol boundary.}
Bibliographic search details, extended comparator tables, diagnostic
protocols, and implementation variants are collected in the supplementary
material; the main article retains only the theorem-by-theorem comparison and
the proof-supporting population covariance certificate below.

The detailed finite-record algorithms, withholding rules, covariance
interfaces, and diagnostic protocols are supplied in the supplementary
material and are not part of the pointwise Theorem~E example.

For Theorem~E, the manuscript certifies only covariance nondegeneracy at the
fixed population point \(z_0=1/2\).  The certificate supports the displayed
projection-limit example and no inferential calibration.

\input{app_diagonal_branch_certificate}

\begin{remark}[Parry comparator in the supplement]
The ideal one-step blanking Parry benchmark is a comparator only.  It is not
part of the D-MAP theorem package and is recorded in the supplementary
material rather than as a main-text theorem or appendix.
\end{remark}

\section*{Data availability}

No empirical data were created or analysed.  The population covariance
certificate is independently replayable from
\texttt{certificates/diagonal\_branch\_certificate.py}; its stored transcript
is \texttt{certificates/diagonal\_branch\_z\_half.json}, and exact commands,
environment versions, scope, and SHA-256 hashes are recorded in
\texttt{certificates/README.md}.  The script uses only the Python standard
library and certifies only \(z_0=1/2\).  No simulations, fits, or validation
data are used as evidence for the theorem statements.

\paragraph{Estimated branch-map reduction.}\label{app:branch-map-oracle-reduction-main}
Work at a separated population point \(p\ne s\), and let \(\mathcal B\) be the
deterministic oracle branch map from
\Cref{conv:branch-map-labelled-rates-main}.  Choose disjoint open
neighbourhoods \(U_p,U_s\subset(0,1)\) of the two population roots on which the
oracle labels are constant.  Let \(\widehat{\mathcal B}_N\) be any branch map
formed from calibration or side data, and let
\[
\mathcal C_N=\{\widehat{\mathcal B}_N
\text{ agrees with }\mathcal B\text{ on }U_p\cup U_s\}.
\]
If \(\PP(\mathcal C_N)\to1\), then every retained labelled-root or
labelled-rate estimator obtained by replacing \(\mathcal B\) with
\(\widehat{\mathcal B}_N\) is asymptotically equivalent to the oracle-labelled
estimator.  In particular, all Gaussian limits, plug-in covariance
consistency statements, and retained-rank Wald limits proved conditionally on
\(\mathcal B\) remain valid for the estimated branch map.  If only the weaker
bound \(\PP(\mathcal C_N^c)\le\epsilon_N\) is available, each corresponding
one-sided coverage lower bound is reduced by at most \(\epsilon_N+o(1)\).

The retained empirical roots converge in probability to the separated
population roots.  Hence, with probability tending to one, the retained roots
lie in \(U_p\cup U_s\).  On the intersection of this event with
\(\mathcal C_N\), the estimated-map and oracle-map labelled estimators are
identical.  Therefore their difference is zero with probability tending to
one, and Slutsky's theorem transfers the oracle Gaussian, covariance, and Wald
limits.  For coverage, the reported event can fail relative to the oracle
event only on \(\mathcal C_N^c\), up to the \(o(1)\) probability that the
retained roots have not entered \(U_p\cup U_s\).  This gives the stated loss
bound.

\subsection{Diagonal branch certificate interface}
\label{app:finite-domain-diagonal-certification-main}
\label{app:diagonal-branch-certificate-protocol-main}
\label{app:finite-projected-gaussian-certificates-main}
\label{app:finite-record-implementation-protocols-main}

The detailed interval-cover verifier, projected-Gaussian quadrature brackets,
canonical DKW simulation rule, and implementation algorithms are supplementary
extension material.  The main article uses only the population branch
interface below to support the ideal fixed-null asymptotic theorem at
\(z_0=1/2\).  It does not print any record-specific finite diagonal transcript.

\begin{remark}[Worked diagonal branch certificate]\label{rem:worked-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}
The printed point transcript for \(z=1/2\) is
\Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  It certifies the
full-rank branch for that single candidate only; it is not a continuum or
neighbouring-point branch classification.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Certified diagonal covariance branch]\label{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}
Fix \(0<z<1\), set \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\), \(t_z=(1,z)^\top\), and form the
actual D-MAP covariance \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  A diagonal branch certificate is
a population certificate for the covariance branch at a fixed candidate.  It
proves exactly one of:
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,
\]
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0,
\]
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z\ne0,
\]
or
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0.
\]
Strict inequalities require a displayed positive margin.  Rank-deficient
branches require exact equalities, either symbolic identities or certified
zero-width interval enclosures.  A floating-point eigenvalue calculation is
not a branch certificate.  A branch certificate alone is not a finite
accept/reject transcript; a realized finite diagonal report also needs the
record-specific statistic enclosure \([Q]\) and critical-value bracket
\([L,U]\), neither of which is printed in the main article.  In the submitted
main article the only printed branch transcript is
the full-rank point certificate at \(z=1/2\) in
\Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}; all other diagonal
candidates are diagnostics unless a separate branch transcript is attached,
and no candidate has an executed finite-report transcript in this article.
\end{definition}

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Outward-rounded diagonal branch certificate]\label{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}
The supplementary protocol evaluates
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main} with directed rounding, records
enclosures for \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\),
\(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\), and \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z\), and accepts a branch
only when those enclosures prove one alternative in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}.  This main-text lemma is the
mathematical interface used by Theorem~E: accepted transcripts certify the
population covariance branch; failed transcripts leave the candidate
diagnostic only.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Supplementary interval-cover branch certification]\label{lem:diagonal-certified-interval-cover-main}
A future finite-domain extension may cover a compact interval
\([z^-,z^+]\Subset(0,1)\) by finitely many certified subintervals.  Each
terminal subinterval must satisfy
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main} with one branch label,
and the transcript must prove that the accepted subintervals cover the stated
domain with no undecided remainder.  If any terminal interval remains
undecided, that part of the domain is not coverage-certified.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{lemma}[D-MAP diagonal covariance alternatives]\label{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}
At each fixed exchange-diagonal population point
\(\sigma_z=(2z,z^2)\), \(0<z<1\), the nonnegative definite matrix
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) satisfies exactly one of four alternatives: full rank,
rank one with range different from \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\), rank one
with range equal to \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\), or zero covariance.  The
tests are
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=2
\Longleftrightarrow \det\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,
\qquad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0
\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,
\]
and, in the remaining rank-one case,
\[
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}
\Longleftrightarrow \Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0 .
\]
The rank-one-normal branch has limiting law
\(\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\chi^2_1\); the zero-covariance branch has an
identically zero limiting statistic.  The full-rank and rank-one non-normal
branches have continuous projected-Gaussian laws and exact lower quantiles.
\end{lemma}

\begin{remark}[Supplementary finite diagonal report protocols]\label{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}\label{prop:finite-diagonal-report-master-main}
Finite diagonal report certificates, projected-Gaussian quantile brackets,
DKW-inflated simulation rules, and the fixed-candidate diagonal calibration
algorithm are not part of the main article's delivered theorem package.  They
are supplementary extension protocols.  The main article prints no
record-specific \([L,U]\), no record-specific \([Q]\), and no candidate-specific
finite comparison tuple.  Therefore the submitted theorem chain ends at
Theorem~E's ideal fixed-null asymptotics and asserts no finite diagonal
accept/reject/undecided output.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Finite-domain diagonal certification for implementation extensions}
\label{app:finite-domain-diagonal-certification-main}

The submitted manuscript uses only the point certificate at \(z=1/2\).  The
following interval-cover verifier is retained as implementation machinery for a
future extension that prints additional point or interval transcripts.  It is
not a paper-level theorem claim for any candidate outside \(z=1/2\).

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Finite interval-cover diagonal branch certification]\label{lem:diagonal-certified-interval-cover-main}
Let \(I=[z^-,z^+]\Subset(0,1)\) be a compact diagonal candidate interval that
is reported as coverage-certified in an implementation extension.  The
deterministic branch verifier is as follows.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item Start with the queue containing \(I\) and with an empty certified list
\(\mathcal C\).
\item Remove one interval \(J\) from the queue.  Apply the outward-rounded
evaluation in \Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main} on the
whole interval \(J\).
\item If exactly one of the four branch tests in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main} succeeds on \(J\), append
\((J,\mathrm{branch})\) to \(\mathcal C\).
\item If no branch test succeeds and the prescribed maximum subdivision depth,
precision budget, or exact-symbolic fallback has not been exhausted, bisect
\(J\) and return the two children to the queue.
\item If no branch test succeeds after the declared resources are exhausted,
append \(J\) to the undecided list \(\mathcal U\).
\end{enumerate}

The extension transcript contains the input interval \(I\), the precision and
rounding mode, every terminal interval, the branch label and margin for every
interval in \(\mathcal C\), the undecided list \(\mathcal U\), and an exact
rational endpoint check proving
\[
I=\bigcup_{(J,\mathrm{branch})\in\mathcal C}J\ \cup\
\bigcup_{J\in\mathcal U}J
\]
with disjoint interiors.  The interval \(I\) is a certified extension interval
only when this verifier returns a finite terminal list and
\(\mathcal U=\varnothing\).  In that case
\[
I=\bigcup_{j=1}^M I_j
\]
and directed interval evaluation proves exactly one branch condition on each
\(I_j\).  Therefore every candidate \(z\in I\) belongs to a certified
subinterval on which the population branch of
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is fixed.  If \(\mathcal U\ne\varnothing\), the union of
the undecided intervals is displayed and those candidates remain diagnostic.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{proof}
All branch assertions made on a terminal interval are consequences of
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}, so each accepted
terminal interval has a proved population branch for every \(z\) in that
interval.  The four branch outcomes in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main} are mutually exclusive for the
actual nonnegative definite matrix \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by
\Cref{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}.  Hence two distinct
branch labels cannot both be valid at the same population point; the verifier
therefore accepts a terminal interval only when its directed enclosures prove a
single outcome uniformly over the interval.

The equality of the endpoint union is a finite rational check in the transcript,
independent of floating-point arithmetic.  When the undecided list is empty,
the accepted terminal intervals cover all of \(I\), and every point in \(I\)
inherits the unique branch proved on the terminal interval containing it.  If
the list is nonempty, no coverage-certified extension is invoked on that
undecided subunion.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Diagonal branch certificates}\label{app:diagonal-branch-certificate-protocol-main}

This subsection contains the finite branch-certificate convention and
outward-rounded verifier used by Theorem~E.  It is implementation certificate
machinery for the analytic covariance alternatives of
\Cref{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}.

\begin{definition}[Certified diagonal covariance branch]\label{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}
Fix \(0<z<1\) and form the actual D-MAP covariance
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by \eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  Put
\[
n_z=(-z,1)^\top,\qquad t_z=(1,z)^\top .
\]
For each reported diagonal candidate \(z\), a diagonal branch certificate at
\(z\) is the following finite object.
It contains:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.2em]
\item an exact description of the input \(z\), or an interval enclosure
\([z]\Subset(0,1)\) if the reported branch is asserted uniformly on that
input interval;
\item an outward-rounded enclosure \([\theta]\) of
\(\theta=-\log z\), or a symbolic identity for \(\theta\);
\item outward-rounded interval enclosures for every scalar arithmetic operation
in \eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main} and
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main};
\item the three outward-rounded branch quantities
\[
[I_{\tau}]\supset \operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z),\qquad
[I_{\det}]\supset \det\Sigma_\sigma(z),\qquad
[w]\supset \Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z,
\]
computed from the enclosed matrix by the directed-rounding formulas in
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}.
\item in the rank-one non-normal branch, an outward-rounded enclosure
\[
[a_{\rm rn}]
\supset
\left(
1-\frac{n_z^\top\Sigma_\sigma(z)n_z}
{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\,\|n_z\|^2}
\right)^2
\]
of the scalar projected-line scale used in
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}.
\end{enumerate}
The certificate transcript printed in the manuscript, or an explicitly
included appendix transcript, must specify the precision, rounding mode, and
the displayed branch margin \(\eta>0\) whenever it asserts a strict positive
inequality.  A repository script may reproduce the transcript, but the
coverage-certified branch status is attached to the printed interval
transcript, not to an undisplayed local file.  This branch transcript is only
one component of a finite diagonal report certificate.  A realized
finite-record accept/reject/undecided output additionally requires the
record-specific critical-value bracket and statistic interval in the tuple
\(\mathcal C(z,\alpha,N)\) of
\Cref{thm:certified-diagonal-inference-main}.  Equalities used to assert a
rank-deficient branch must be exact equalities, either symbolic identities or
interval enclosures of width zero in the certified arithmetic; a small
floating-point residual is not an equality certificate.

The four admissible certified outcomes are:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item \textbf{Full rank.}  The certificate proves
\[
[I_{\det}]\subset[\eta,\infty).
\]
\item \textbf{Rank one, normal range.}  The certificate proves
\[
[I_{\det}]=[0,0],\qquad
[I_{\tau}]\subset[\eta,\infty),\qquad
[w]=\{(0,0)^\top\}.
\]
\item \textbf{Rank one, non-normal range.}  The certificate proves
\[
[I_{\det}]=[0,0],\qquad
[I_{\tau}]\subset[\eta,\infty),\qquad
[q]\subset[\eta,\infty),
\]
where \([q]\) is the outward-rounded enclosure of
\(\|w\|^2=w_1^2+w_2^2\) obtained from \([w]\), and also supplies
\([a_{\rm rn}]\Subset(0,1]\).
\item \textbf{Zero covariance.}  The certificate proves
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0
\]
entrywise, equivalently \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0\) for this
nonnegative definite matrix.
\end{enumerate}
If none of these certificates is available, the diagonal rank branch is
declared inconclusive.  An inconclusive branch may still be used to display the
projected-Gaussian diagnostic \(Q_N(z)\) and the ideal conditional quantile,
but it is not a coverage-certified report in Theorem~E.  Conversely, even a
conclusive branch certificate is not by itself a finite decision transcript:
it must be paired with \([L,U]\) and \([Q]\) in
\(\mathcal C(z,\alpha,N)\).

The certification convention is deliberately finite.  This paper does not use
an unproved global analytic sign classification of
\(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) on \(0<z<1\), and a floating-point eigenvalue
calculation at a candidate is not a substitute for a certificate.  The worked
certificate in \Cref{rem:worked-diagonal-branch-certificate-main} supplies only
the single submitted candidate \(z=1/2\); no continuum branch classification
and no neighbouring-point certificate is inferred from it.  The finite-domain
interval-cover machinery needed for a later implementation extension is not
part of the paper-level theorem and is recorded in
\Cref{app:finite-domain-diagonal-certification-main}.
\end{definition}

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Outward-rounded diagonal branch certificate]\label{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}
For a fixed point \(0<z<1\), or for a closed input interval
\([z]\Subset(0,1)\), the branch certificate in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main} is reproducibly obtained from
the finite formulas of \Cref{prop:computable-diagonal-covariance-main} as
follows.
Work in an interval arithmetic system with directed rounding.  Enclose the
input by \([z]\), enclose \(\theta=-\log z\) over that whole input enclosure by
\([\theta]\), and then evaluate the displayed formulas
\[
[g_0]=(1-[z])-[\theta][z],
\qquad
[g_1]=[z]\{(1-[z])(1+[\theta])-[\theta][z]\},
\]
\[
[\mu]=\frac1{1-[z]}+\frac{[\theta][z]}{(1-[z])^2},
\qquad
[\nu]=\frac{1+[z]}{(1-[z])^2}
     +\frac{[\theta][z](3+[z])}{(1-[z])^3},
\qquad
[m_2]=[g_1]+[g_0]^2.
\]
Set
\[
[r]=\frac1{[\mu]}(1,[g_0],[m_2])^\top
\]
and form the interval matrices \([A_z]\), \([B_z]\) and interval vectors
\([e_z]\), \([d_z]\) from the displayed formulas immediately preceding
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main}.  Directed evaluation of
\[
[\Sigma_r]=\frac1{[\mu]}\left\{
[A_z]-[e_z][r]^\top-[r][e_z]^\top+[\nu][r][r]^\top
+[B_z]-[d_z][r]^\top+[B_z]^\top-[r][d_z]^\top
\right\}
\]
encloses the regenerative covariance.
Next compute the quotient-Jacobian interval \([J_\Phi]\) from
\eqref{eq:lambda-gradient-main}--\eqref{eq:phi-jacobian-main}, with every
division checked to have a denominator interval not containing zero, and put
\[
[\Sigma]=[J_\Phi]\,[\Sigma_r]\,[J_\Phi]^\top .
\]
Writing
\[
[\Sigma]=\begin{pmatrix}
[a]&[b]\\
[c]&[d]
\end{pmatrix},
\]
the branch quantities required by \Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}
are not optional diagnostics but the certificate data:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal-branch-interval-quantities-main}
[I_{\tau}]=[a]+[d],\qquad
[I_{\det}]=[a][d]-[b][c],\qquad
[w]=
\binom{[a]+[z][b]}{[c]+[z][d]},
\qquad
[q]=[w_1]^2+[w_2]^2 .
\end{equation}
For a rank-one non-normal outcome, also compute the scalar-law enclosure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal-rank-one-nonnormal-scale-certificate-main}
[a_{\rm rn}]
=\left(
1-\frac{[n]^\top[\Sigma][n]}{[I_{\tau}]\,([z]^2+1)}
\right)^2,
\qquad [n]=(-[z],1)^\top .
\end{equation}
If the intervals in \eqref{eq:diagonal-branch-interval-quantities-main}
satisfy one of the four certified outcomes in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}, then the corresponding
population branch of \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is proved for the fixed candidate,
or uniformly for every candidate in the certified input interval.  If none of
the interval separations succeeds, the branch is reported as inconclusive.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{proof}
The formulas for \(g_0,g_1,\mu,\nu,m_2,r,A_z,e_z,d_z,B_z\) are exactly the
finite D-MAP covariance formulas of
\Cref{prop:computable-diagonal-covariance-main}.  Directed interval arithmetic
is inclusion isotone for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division
by an interval excluding zero.  Therefore each displayed interval contains the
corresponding real scalar or matrix entry.  The quotient denominator is
nonzero at every fixed diagonal point by
\eqref{eq:diagonal-quotient-denominator-main}, so sufficiently sharp input
enclosures make the Jacobian divisions certified.  The sandwich product then
contains the real covariance
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)=D\Phi(r(z))\Sigma_r(z)D\Phi(r(z))^\top\).  Finally,
\eqref{eq:diagonal-branch-interval-quantities-main} is precisely the directed
interval evaluation of
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\), \(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\),
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)(1,z)^\top\), and its squared norm.  Interval exclusion from
zero proves the stated strict inequalities, while a zero-width interval or a
symbolic identity proves the asserted equalities.  The branch conclusion is
then the \(2\times2\) nonnegative-definite rank/range classification of
\Cref{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}.  In the rank-one
non-normal case, write
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\lambda vv^\top\), \(\lambda>0\), \(\|v\|=1\).  Since
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\lambda\),
\[
\frac{n_z^\top\Sigma_\sigma(z)n_z}
{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\|n_z\|^2}
=\frac{(n_z^\top v)^2}{\|n_z\|^2},
\]
so \eqref{eq:diagonal-rank-one-nonnormal-scale-certificate-main} encloses the
scale \(a(z,v)\) in
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Worked diagonal branch certificate]\label{rem:worked-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}
The self-contained certificate used by this manuscript is the interval
transcript in \Cref{app:self-contained-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  The
paper-local script, stored JSON transcript, replay environment, command lines,
and transcript hash are supplementary reproducibility material.  The main
article uses only the printed interval transcript and its proved determinant
margin.  The accepted arithmetic is base-ten decimal interval arithmetic with
precision \(90\) significant digits and directed rounding downward for every
lower endpoint and upward for every upper endpoint; the input interval and all
branch enclosures are printed in
\Cref{app:self-contained-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  Thus the
certificate used below is tied to the printed formulas rather than to a
rounded midpoint table.

For this point certificate the exact substitution into
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main} is
\[
z=\frac12,\qquad
\theta=\log2,\qquad
g_0=\frac{1-\log2}{2},\qquad
g_1=\frac14,
\]
\[
\mu=2+2\log2,\qquad
m_2=g_1+g_0^2 .
\]
Substituting these values in \eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main} and
then in
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)=D\Phi(r(z))\Sigma_r(z)D\Phi(r(z))^\top\), the directed
interval transcript encloses the entries of \(\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)\) as follows:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma_{11}&\in[25.0645227916080864,25.0645227916080865],\\
\Sigma_{12}&\in[17.2222593244352288,17.2222593244352289],\\
\Sigma_{21}&\in[17.2222593244352288,17.2222593244352289],\\
\Sigma_{22}&\in[11.8884649865292259,11.8884649865292260].
\end{aligned}
\]
The branch decision uses these outward-rounded intervals directly; no rounded
midpoint matrix is used in the certificate.
\[
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\doteq 36.9529877781373,
\qquad
\det\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\doteq 1.37248537400032.
\]
The appendix transcript records outward-rounded enclosures of all these
displayed quantities; in short display form, the corresponding branch
intervals are
\[
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\in[36.95298777813731,36.95298777813732],
\]
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\in[1.372485374000321,1.372485374000322].
\]
These two intervals are deliberately rounded outward for compact display; the
full precision determinant, trace, matrix, tangent-vector, rounding-mode, and
input intervals are part of the manuscript in
\Cref{app:self-contained-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  The determinant
enclosure is separated from zero, so the certificate proves the full-rank
branch with margin, for instance, \(\eta=1.37\).  The same transcript
also records the outward-rounded vector enclosure for
\(\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)(1,1/2)^\top\); it is not needed for the full-rank
decision but is included because the branch protocol always records the
tangent-direction test.
This is a point certificate only: it certifies the full-rank branch for the
single reported candidate \(z=1/2\), not for neighbouring \(z\)'s and not for
the continuum \(0<z<1\).
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[D-MAP diagonal covariance alternatives]\label{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}
Work at a fixed constrained D-MAP exchange-diagonal population point
\(\sigma_z=(2z,z^2)\), \(0<z<1\), and form the actual diagonal covariance
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by the finite formula
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  Let \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\).  Exactly
one of the following mutually exclusive
alternatives holds:
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=2,
\]
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\ne\operatorname{span}\{n_z\},
\]
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\operatorname{span}\{n_z\},
\]
or
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0 .
\]
The first two alternatives have a continuous projected-Gaussian statistic and
therefore supply exact-level projected-Gaussian cases for all confidence
levels.  In the third alternative the limiting statistic has law
\(\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\chi^2_1\): its distribution function is
\(1/2+F_{\chi^2_1}(t)/2\) for \(t>0\).  Hence its lower \(p_c\)-quantile is
zero for \(p_c\le1/2\), but for \(p_c>1/2\) it is
\(F_{\chi^2_1}^{-1}(2p_c-1)\) and is continuous.  The
fourth alternative has an identically zero limiting statistic.  The occurrence
of the covariance alternative is not a modelling choice: it is obtained by
evaluating the finite matrix
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  The paper does not prove a
closed-form analytic sign classification of this determinant for every
\(0<z<1\).  Therefore the operational diagonal coverage branches in
Theorem~E are conditional on the certified population branch in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}, operationally generated by
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}, not on a global
closed-form \(z\)-classification and not on an uncertified floating-point rank
label.  In
the rank-one-normal covariance
alternative, the theorem-level branch still depends on the requested quantile
level \(p_c=1-\alpha\): exact unbuffered coverage for \(p_c>1/2\),
and buffered conservative coverage for \(p_c\le1/2\).

Equivalently, because \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is \(2\times2\) and nonnegative
definite, these cases are checked directly from the actual D-MAP covariance by
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,
\]
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,
\]
and, with \(t_z=(1,z)^\top\) tangent to the exchange diagonal,
\[
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0 .
\]
The remaining case
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z\ne0
\]
is the rank-one non-normal exact-level alternative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The matrix \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is a \(2\times2\) nonnegative definite matrix
because it is obtained by sandwiching the nonnegative definite regenerative
covariance \(\Sigma_r(z)\) with the deterministic Jacobian \(D\Phi(r(z))\).
Thus its rank is \(0\), \(1\), or \(2\).  In rank one its range is a single
line, which is either the normal line \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\) or is not
that line.  These alternatives are exhaustive and mutually exclusive.

For a \(2\times2\) nonnegative definite matrix, full rank is equivalent to
positive determinant, and the zero matrix is equivalent to zero trace.  In the
remaining rank-one case, \(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0\) and
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0\).  Since
\(t_z=(1,z)^\top\) spans the tangent line orthogonal to \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\),
the range is \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\) exactly when the kernel is the
tangent line, equivalently \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0\).  If this kernel test
fails, the rank-one range is not the normal line.  The statements about
continuity, the half-mass at zero, and the zero statistic are precisely
\Cref{thm:projected-gaussian-continuity-degeneracy-main} applied to
\(\Sigma=\Sigma_\sigma(z)\).  The certificate definition is only the same
case analysis written as a reproducible branch-selection rule: each positive
inequality gives the displayed margin, and each asserted rank deficiency is
accepted only when the corresponding equality has been proved exactly.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Model verification.}
We now specialize the generic renewal tools to the standing record experiment
of \Cref{ass:fixed-sampled-boundary-record-main}.  The exponential-tail lemma
verifies the renewal hypothesis for this model.  Theorem~C then states the
exact finite-record statistic for the three inclusion coordinates and applies
the generic complete-cycle CLT to that statistic.

\begin{maintheorem}[Compact-uniform singular exchange experiment]
\label{thm:singular-exchange-limit-experiment-main}
Let \(\mathcal K\Subset(0,1)\) and \(H<\infty\).  Denote by
\(P_{p,s}^{(N)}\) the law of the stationary visible record
\((A_1,\ldots,A_N)\) under the sampled-counter model with survival factors
\((p,s)\).  For \(z\in\mathcal K\), \(|h|\le H\), and all sufficiently large

\[
 p_{N,z,h}=z+hN^{-1/4},\qquad
 s_{N,z,h}=z-hN^{-1/4},\qquad
 P_{N,z,h}=P_{p_{N,z,h},s_{N,z,h}}^{(N)}.
\tag{SE1}
\]
At the diagonal let
\[
 D_z(k)=1-z+\log z\{kz-k+z\},\qquad
 g_z(k)=z^kD_z(k),\qquad k\ge0,
\tag{SE2}

\begin{paperthm}[Pointwise exchange-diagonal projection example]\label{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main}
Fix
\[
z_0=\frac12,\qquad \sigma_0=(1,1/4),\qquad
H_{z_0}=\{h\in\mathbb R^2:h_2\le z_0h_1\},
\]
and let \(F=\{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2):\sigma_2\le\sigma_1^2/4\}\).  Suppose the
true population satisfies \(\sigma=\sigma_0\), the printed interval
certificate proves
\(\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma_\sigma(z_0)\}>0.037\), and
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat\sigma_N^{\rm raw}-\sigma_0)
\Rightarrow Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\sigma(z_0)).
\]
Let \(\Pi_F\) be the locally unique Euclidean projection, with any fixed
measurable tie rule outside the local neighbourhood, and set
\[
\widehat\sigma_N=\Pi_F(\widehat\sigma_N^{\rm raw}),\qquad
X_N=\sqrt N(\widehat\sigma_N-\sigma_0).
\]
Then
\[
X_N\Rightarrow \Pi_{H_{z_0}}Z .
\]
This theorem is only a pointwise projection example at the preselected point
\(z_0=1/2\).  It defines no statistic for testing, no simulated or limiting
critical value, no confidence region, and no feasible or oracle coverage
claim.  Selection of \(z_0\) from the data and uniformity over \(0<z<1\) are
outside its scope.
\end{paperthm}

\begin{proof}
Near \(\sigma_0\), the boundary of \(F\) is the smooth graph
\(\sigma_2=\sigma_1^2/4\), whose tangent cone at \(\sigma_0\) is
\(H_{z_0}\).  The standard first-order metric-projection expansion at a smooth
inequality boundary is
\[
\sqrt N\{\Pi_F(\sigma_0+N^{-1/2}h_N)-\sigma_0\}
=\Pi_{H_{z_0}}h_N+o(1)
\]
for every bounded convergent sequence \(h_N\)
\cite{Shapiro1987MetricProjection}.  Tightness of the raw quotient CLT permits
the expansion on events with probability tending to one.  Slutsky's theorem
and continuity of projection onto the closed half-space give the asserted
limit.  The certificate establishes only that the covariance in this limit is
nonsingular; it is not used to calibrate a procedure.
\end{proof}

\begin{maintheorem}[Compact-uniform singular exchange experiment]
\label{thm:singular-exchange-limit-experiment-main}
Let \(\mathcal K\Subset(0,1)\) and \(H<\infty\).  Denote by
\(P_{p,s}^{(N)}\) the law of the stationary visible record
\((A_1,\ldots,A_N)\) under the sampled-counter model with survival factors
\((p,s)\).  For \(z\in\mathcal K\), \(|h|\le H\), and all sufficiently large
\(N\), put
\[
 p_{N,z,h}=z+hN^{-1/4},\qquad
 s_{N,z,h}=z-hN^{-1/4},\qquad
 P_{N,z,h}=P_{p_{N,z,h},s_{N,z,h}}^{(N)}.
\tag{SE1}
\]
At the diagonal let
\[
 D_z(k)=1-z+\log z\{kz-k+z\},\qquad
 g_z(k)=z^kD_z(k),\qquad k\ge0,
\tag{SE2}
\]
and define
\[
\begin{split}
B_z(k)=\frac{z^{k-2}}6\bigl[&
k^3(z-1)\log z+3k^2\{\log z+1-z\}\\
&-3kz\log z-6kz-2z\log z-3z\bigr],
\qquad b_z(k)=\frac{B_z(k)}{g_z(k)} .
\end{split}
\tag{SE3}
\]
Then \(g_z\) is the diagonal Palm gap mass and
\[
 g_{z+d,z-d}(k)=g_z(k)+d^2B_z(k)+O(d^4)
\tag{SE4}
\]
for every \(k\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sum_{k\ge0}g_z(k)b_z(k)=0,\qquad
 \mu_z=\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)g_z(k)
 =\frac{1-z-z\log z}{(1-z)^2},
\tag{SE5}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal I(z)=\frac1{\mu_z}
 \sum_{k\ge0}g_z(k)b_z(k)^2
 =\frac1{\mu_z}\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{B_z(k)^2}{g_z(k)}
\tag{SE6}
\]
is finite, strictly positive, and continuous on \((0,1)\).

Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and write the complete gaps as
\(G_{1,N},\ldots,G_{K_N,N}\).  Set
\[
 \Delta_{N,z}=\frac1{\sqrt N}
 \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_z(G_{j,N}).
\tag{SE7}
\]
Uniformly for \(z\in\mathcal K\),
\[
 \Delta_{N,z}\ \Longrightarrow\
 \mathcal N\{0,\mathcal I(z)\}
\tag{SE8}
\]
in bounded-Lipschitz distance under \(P_{N,z,0}\).  More precisely, for every
\(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\sup_{\substack{z\in\mathcal K\\ |h|\le H}}
P_{N,z,0}\!\left(
\left|
\log\frac{dP_{N,z,h}}{dP_{N,z,0}}
-h^2\Delta_{N,z}
+\frac12h^4\mathcal I(z)
\right|>\varepsilon
\right)\longrightarrow0 .
\tag{SE9}
\]
Consequently the likelihood-ratio processes, indexed by \(|h|\le H\),
converge uniformly over \(z\in\mathcal K\) to the scalar Gaussian experiments
\[
 X_z\sim\mathcal N\!\left(h^2\sqrt{\mathcal I(z)},1\right),
\qquad |h|\le H.
\tag{SE10}
\]
Equivalently, under \(P_{N,z,h}\),
\[
 \Delta_{N,z}\Longrightarrow
 \mathcal N\{h^2\mathcal I(z),\mathcal I(z)\}
\tag{SE11}
\]
uniformly over \(z\in\mathcal K\) and bounded \(h\).
The limit identifies \(h^2\), not the sign of \(h\).  This is the complete
singular experiment for the specified path; it is not an ordered hidden-label
experiment.
\end{maintheorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(x=-\log p\), \(y=-\log s\).  The Palm gap formula in Theorem~A is
\[
 g_{p,s}(k)
 =\frac{y(1-p)p^k-x(1-s)s^k}{y-x},
\tag{SE12}
\]
with its continuous value when \(p=s\).  Substitute \(p=z+d\) and \(s=z-d\)
and expand the even analytic function of \(d\).  The constant and quadratic
coefficients are exactly \textup{(SE2)} and \textup{(SE3)}, proving
\textup{(SE4)}.  The diagonal survival tail is
\[
 S_z(k)=z^k(1-k\log z).
\]
Thus \(g_z(k)=S_z(k)-S_z(k+1)\), which proves the first identity in
\textup{(SE2)} and, by summing the tails, the formula for \(\mu_z\).
Differentiating \(\sum_kg_{z+d,z-d}(k)=1\) at order \(d^2\) gives
\(\sum_kB_z(k)=0\), hence the centring in \textup{(SE5)}.

On every \(\mathcal K\Subset(0,1)\), the masses in \textup{(SE12)} and all
their derivatives through any fixed order have a common
\(C(1+k)^m r^k\) envelope for some \(r<1\).  Termwise differentiation and
summation are therefore valid uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).  Formula
\textup{(SE3)} gives \(|b_z(k)|\le C_{\mathcal K}(1+k)^2\), so
\textup{(SE6)} is finite and continuous.  It is positive: if it vanished,
then \(B_z(k)=0\) for every \(k\).  But
\[
 B_z(0)=-\frac{2\log z+3}{6z};
\]
its only zero is \(z=e^{-3/2}\), and at that point the numerator in
\textup{(SE3)} for \(k=1\) equals \(-6z\), so \(B_z(1)\ne0\).

Put \(q=d^2\).  Uniform analytic differentiation in the symmetric coordinate
\((p+s,ps)=(2z,z^2-q)\) gives
\[
 g_{z+\sqrt q,z-\sqrt q}(k)
 =g_z(k)\{1+qb_z(k)+q^2c_z(k)+q^3R_{z,q}(k)\},
\tag{SE13}
\]
where \(\sum_kg_z(k)c_z(k)=0\) and \(c_z,R_{z,q}\) have common polynomial
envelopes on \(\mathcal K\) for \(q\) in a fixed right neighbourhood of zero.
The same statement follows directly from \textup{(SE12)}.  Uniform
exponential gap tails imply
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le K_N}G_{j,N}=O_{P_{N,z,0}}(\log N)
\tag{SE14}
\]
uniformly in \(z\in\mathcal K\).  Taylor expansion of the logarithm in
\textup{(SE13)}, on the event in \textup{(SE14)}, therefore gives uniformly
for \(|h|\le H\), with \(q=h^2N^{-1/2}\),
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\log
\frac{g_{z+\sqrt q,z-\sqrt q}(G_{j,N})}{g_z(G_{j,N})}
={}&h^2\Delta_{N,z}\\
&+\frac{h^4}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
\{c_z(G_{j,N})-\tfrac12b_z(G_{j,N})^2\}+o_P(1).
\end{split}
\tag{SE15}
\]

Under the diagonal law the complete Palm gaps are consecutive i.i.d.
variables with mass \(g_z\), and the renewal count satisfies
\(K_N/N\to1/\mu_z\).  The uniform regenerative law of large numbers applied
to the two polynomially bounded rewards in \textup{(SE15)} makes its second
line converge to \(-h^4\mathcal I(z)/2\), uniformly on
\(\mathcal K\times[-H,H]\).  The uniform regenerative central limit theorem
applied to \(b_z\) proves \textup{(SE8)}.  Both results can also be obtained by
the subsequence criterion: every sequence \(z_N\in\mathcal K\) has a
convergent subsequence, and the common exponential envelope supplies
Lindeberg, renewal-count replacement, and uniform integrability along that
subsequence.

It remains to compare the product of complete-gap likelihoods with the
stationary \(N\)-bin likelihood.  Their ratio contains only the left
equilibrium-delay factor, the right censored-tail factor, and the normalizing
cycle mean.  Their logarithmic \(q\)-derivatives have polynomial envelopes in
the two endpoint lengths.  Those lengths are \(O_P(\log N)\) uniformly by the
same exponential-tail bound, so their total log-likelihood contribution is
\(O_P(N^{-1/2}\operatorname{polylog}N)=o_P(1)\).  This proves
\textup{(SE9)}.

The right side of \textup{(SE9)} is a continuous function of \(h\) and the
remainder is uniform on the compact index set.  Hence the likelihood-ratio
processes converge in \(C([-H,H])\) to
\[
 h\longmapsto
 \exp\{h^2\sqrt{\mathcal I(z)}\,Z-\tfrac12h^4\mathcal I(z)\},
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
which is \textup{(SE10)}.  Le Cam's third lemma gives \textup{(SE11)}.
Finally,
\[
\sqrt N\{(p_{N,z,h}+s_{N,z,h},p_{N,z,h}s_{N,z,h})
-(2z,z^2)\}=(0,-h^2),
\]
which explains both the \(N^{-1/4}\) scale and the loss of the sign.  General
locally conic and loss-of-identifiability asymptotics are established in
\cite{DacunhaCastelleGassiat1997LocallyConic,
LiuShao2003LossIdentifiability}; the calculation above is the
compact-uniform stationary-renewal specialization.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete Markov--Palm tangent space and pointwise omnibus score]
\label{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main}
Fix $0<\alpha<1$, an interior exchange point $\theta_0=(x_0,x_0)$, and let
$g=(g_k)_{k\geq0}$ be its Palm zero-gap law.  Thus $g_k>0$,
$\mu=\sum_{k\geq0}(k+1)g_k<\infty$, and, for this sampled-counter law,
$g$ has an exponential tail.  Put
\[
 \mathsf H=L^2(g\otimes g),\qquad
 \mathsf H_{\rm int}=\{q\in\mathsf H:
 \EE(q\mid G_0)=\EE(q\mid G_1)=0\},
\]
where $G_0,G_1$ are independent with law $g$, and define
\[
 \mathsf T=\{q\in\mathsf H_{\rm int}:q(0,0)=0\}.
 \tag{H}
\]
Consider all quadratic-mean differentiable Markov-gap paths
\[
 Q_t(\ell\mid k)=g_\ell w_t(k,\ell),\qquad w_0=1,
 \qquad \left\|\frac{2(\sqrt{w_t}-1)}t-q\right\|_{\mathsf H}
 \longrightarrow0,
\tag{I}
\]
whose rows sum to one, for which $gQ_t=g$, and which preserve
$(r_0,r_1,r_2)$ to first order.  Then the following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The closed tangent space of these paths is exactly $\mathsf T$; in
particular it is infinite dimensional.  If
\[
 u_0(k)=\mathbf1_{\{k=0\}}-g_0,\qquad
 v_0(k,\ell)=u_0(k)u_0(\ell),
\]
then
\[
 \mathsf T=\mathsf H_{\rm int}\ominus\operatorname{span}\{v_0\}.
 \tag{J}
\]
Every $q\in\mathsf T$ is realized by a two-sided path in \textup{(I)} whose
kernels satisfy a Doeblin minorization by $(1-o(1))g$ and preserve $g$ and
all three inclusion coordinates exactly.  A nonzero such path is nonrenewal
for all sufficiently small nonzero $t$.

\item Every adjacent-pair score generated by a quadratic-mean differentiable
renewal marginal path belongs to the closed span of
$s(G_0)+s(G_1)$, with $s\in L^2_0(g)$.  Hence the sampled-counter renewal
nuisance space is orthogonal to $\mathsf T$.  On the ambient space
$\mathsf H$, the efficient information operator for the Markov interaction
is
\[
 \mathcal I_{\rm eff}=\mu^{-1}\Pi_{\mathsf T},
 \tag{K}
\]
where
\[
 \Pi_{\mathsf T}f=f-\EE(f\mid G_0)-\EE(f\mid G_1)+\EE f
 -\frac{\langle f,v_0\rangle_{\mathsf H}}
 {\|v_0\|_{\mathsf H}^2}v_0.
 \tag{L}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \ker\mathcal I_{\rm eff}
 =\mathsf H_{\rm int}^{\perp}\oplus\operatorname{span}\{v_0\},
 \qquad
 \left.\mathcal I_{\rm eff}\right|_{\mathsf T}
 =\mu^{-1}I_{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{M}
\]

\item Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles from a stationary record and
write its complete gaps as $G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}$, where
$K_N/N\to_P\mu^{-1}$.  For $q\in\mathsf T$, let
\[
 \Delta_N(q)=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{K_N-1}q(G_i,G_{i+1}).
\]
For each fixed finite collection $q_1,\ldots,q_d\in\mathsf T$, the null
joint limit is centred Gaussian with covariance
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\operatorname{Cov}
 \{\Delta_N(q_a),\Delta_N(q_b)\}
 =\mu^{-1}\langle q_a,q_b\rangle_{\mathsf H}.
 \tag{N}
\]
Along the realizing paths constructed in part~\textup{(i)}, or any other
such path whose retained-record endpoint log likelihood is $o_{P_0}(1)$,
the score $q$, evaluated at $t_N=N^{-1/2}$, satisfies
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{N,q}}{dP_{N,0}}
 =\Delta_N(q)-\frac1{2\mu}\|q\|_{\mathsf H}^2+o_{P_0}(1).
 \tag{O}
\]
Thus the limit is the isonormal process on $\mathsf T$ with covariance
\textup{(N)}, rather than a $\mathsf T$-valued normal random element with
identity covariance.  No uniform-LAN assertion over arbitrary norm-compact
subsets of $\mathsf T$ is made.

\item Put
\[
 e_0(k)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\{k=0\}}-g_0}{\sqrt{g_0(1-g_0)}}
\]
and choose a bounded orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2,\ldots$ of
$L^2_0(g)\cap\{e_0\}^{\perp}$.  Enumerate
\[
 \{e_a\otimes e_b:a,b\geq0,\ (a,b)\neq(0,0)\}
 =\{\phi_1,\phi_2,\ldots\};
\]
this is an orthonormal basis of $\mathsf T$.  Fix strictly positive weights
$\lambda_j$ satisfying
\[
 \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j<\infty,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j\|\phi_j\|_\infty^2<\infty,
 \tag{P}
\]
and any deterministic $J_N\uparrow\infty$.  Put
\[
 \widehat\mu_N=
 \begin{cases}
 K_N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{K_N}(G_i+1),&K_N\geq1,\\
 1,&K_N=0,
 \end{cases}
\]
and define, when $K_N\geq2$,
\[
 Z_{j,N}=\sqrt{\frac{\widehat\mu_N}{N}}
 \sum_{i=1}^{K_N-1}\phi_j(G_i,G_{i+1}),\qquad
 Q_N=\sum_{j=1}^{J_N}\lambda_jZ_{j,N}^2,
 \tag{Q}
\]
and put $Q_N=0$ otherwise.  If $\zeta_j$ are independent standard normals,
then
\[
 Q_N\Rightarrow Q_0:=\sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j\zeta_j^2.
 \tag{R}
\]
Let $c_{\alpha,\lambda}$ be the $(1-\alpha)$ quantile of $Q_0$.  Under the
local direction $q=\sum_jq_j\phi_j\in\mathsf T$ along one of the paths
admitted in \textup{(O)},
\[
 Q_N\Rightarrow
 \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j
 \left(\zeta_j+\frac{q_j}{\sqrt\mu}\right)^2.
 \tag{S}
\]
Consequently the test
$\psi_N=\mathbf1_{\{Q_N>c_{\alpha,\lambda}\}}$ has limiting power strictly
larger than $\alpha$ for every fixed $q\in\mathsf T\setminus\{0\}$.

\item The null calibration in \textup{(R)} is stable along the exchange
boundary in the following explicit local sense.  Let
$\sigma=(p+s,ps)$ be the symmetric sampled-counter coordinate and, for fixed
$C<\infty$, let $\sigma_N$ range over null sequences satisfying
\[
 \|\sqrt N(\sigma_N-\sigma_0)\|\leq C.
 \tag{T}
\]
Use in \textup{(Q)} the basis fixed at $\sigma_0$ and the displayed
$\widehat\mu_N$.  Then
\[
 \sup_{\sigma_N:\,\textup{(T)}}
 \left|\PP_{\sigma_N}(Q_N>c_{\alpha,\lambda})-\alpha\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{U}
\]
This class includes exchange-root splittings
$N^{1/4}|p_N-s_N|=O(1)$ provided their symmetric coordinates obey
\textup{(T)}.
\end{enumerate}

The algebraic assertions in parts~\textup{(i)}--\textup{(ii)} use only full
support of $g$, finite $\mu$, and square-integrability of each local score.
For the explicit realizing paths, the uniform density-ratio bound controls
the endpoint terms in parts~\textup{(iii)}--\textup{(iv)}.  The
sampled-counter exponential tail and analytic dependence on $\sigma$ are used
in part~\textup{(v)} for its uniform triangular-array statement.  No claim
that finite mean alone controls the endpoints of every quadratic-mean
differentiable stationary-record path is made.

Generic basis tests of serial independence, Hilbert-space central limit
theorems, and Gaussian-shift arguments are established methods
\cite{SkaugTjostheim1993SerialIndependence,
DedeckerMerlevede2003HilbertCLT,vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
The assertions here are restricted to the sampled-counter Markov--Palm
interaction: the additional atom constraint in \textup{(H)}, its information
projection, and the exchange-boundary calibration of \textup{(Q)}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}

\[
 \sum_\ell g_\ell w_t(k,\ell)=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_k g_kw_t(k,\ell)=1.
\]
Differentiating in quadratic mean gives the two conditional-mean constraints

order is equivalent to $q(0,0)=0$.

\[
 \langle q,v_0\rangle_{\mathsf H}=g_0^2q(0,0),
\]
which proves \textup{(J)} and \textup{(L)}.  To prove realizability, truncate

\]
A renewal marginal perturbation contributes only its one-gap score at the two
ends of an adjacent pair.  It is therefore orthogonal to $\mathsf T$.
Under the null, successive interaction rewards have zero lag-one covariance:
\[
 \EE\{q_a(G_0,G_1)q_b(G_1,G_2)\}=0.
\]
The number of complete cycles per calendar bin tends to $\mu^{-1}$, so the
information quadratic form is $\mu^{-1}\|q\|_{\mathsf H}^2$.  Projection
onto the admissible interaction scores proves \textup{(K)}--\textup{(M)}.

For each fixed finite collection of scores, the one-dependent central limit
theorem and random-index replacement prove \textup{(N)}.  For the realizing
paths in part~\textup{(i)}, the bound
$|t|\|q_{m(t)}\|_\infty\to0$ also makes the endpoint log likelihood
negligible.  Quadratic-mean differentiability then gives \textup{(O)}; the
same conclusion holds under the alternative endpoint hypothesis stated in
part~\textup{(iii)}.  This proves the finite-dimensional local experiment.
Identity covariance on the
infinite-dimensional space is not trace class, so the limit can only be
interpreted cylindrically as the displayed isonormal process.

The normalized $e_0$ is proportional to $u_0$.  Tensoring an orthonormal
basis of $L^2_0(g)$ gives an orthonormal basis of
$\mathsf H_{\rm int}$, and deleting $e_0\otimes e_0$ imposes \textup{(J)}.
Condition \textup{(P)} makes
\[
 \bigl(\sqrt{\lambda_j}\phi_j(G_i,G_{i+1})\bigr)_{j\geq1}
\]
a square-integrable, one-dependent $\ell^2$-valued random variable.  Its
lag-one covariance vanishes by double centring.  The Hilbert-space central
limit theorem, random-index replacement, and truncation in $J_N$ therefore
give \textup{(R)}.  Joint convergence with the likelihood score and the third
lemma give \textup{(S)}.  If $q\neq0$, some $q_j\neq0$; for every positive
threshold the square of a normal with nonzero mean strictly stochastically
dominates a central normal square.  Conditioning on the remaining independent
coordinates proves strict power because every $\lambda_j$ is positive.

It remains to prove the uniform calibration in \textup{(U)}.  We give the
truncation argument because covariance convergence alone is not a
triangular-array Hilbert-space CLT.  Write
\[
 g_N=g_{\sigma_N},\qquad \delta_N=g_N-g .
\]
Analyticity in the symmetric coordinate and the locally uniform exponential
tail give, uniformly under \textup{(T)},
\[
 \|\delta_N\|_1=O(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \mu_N-\mu=O(N^{-1/2}),
\tag{U1}
\]
together with a common exponential moment for the gap laws \(g_N\).
Introduce the weighted feature
\[
 \Psi(k,\ell)=
 \bigl(\sqrt{\lambda_j}\phi_j(k,\ell)\bigr)_{j\ge1}\in\ell^2,
\qquad
 B_\lambda^2=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j\|\phi_j\|_\infty^2<\infty .
\tag{U2}
\]
Thus \(\|\Psi(k,\ell)\|_{\ell^2}\le B_\lambda\) for every pair.  Since every
\(\phi_j\) is double centred under \(g\),
\[
\begin{split}
 m_N:=\EE_{g_N\otimes g_N}\Psi
 &=\sum_{j\ge1}\sqrt{\lambda_j}
 \langle\phi_j,\delta_N\otimes\delta_N\rangle\,\mathbf e_j,\\
 \|m_N\|_{\ell^2}
 &\le B_\lambda\|\delta_N\|_1^2=O(N^{-1}).
\end{split}
\tag{U3}
\]
This displays, rather than assumes, the cancellation of the two first-order
marginal terms.

Fix \(J\).  The first \(J\) coordinates of
\(\Psi(G_i,G_{i+1})-m_N\) form a uniformly bounded one-dependent triangular
array.  Its lag-zero covariance tends to
\(\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_J)\), while its two lag-one
covariances tend to zero: at \(g\) they vanish exactly by double centring, and
\textup{(U1)} controls the perturbation.  The fixed-dimensional
one-dependent triangular-array CLT therefore gives
\[
 (Z_{1,N},\ldots,Z_{J,N})
 \Longrightarrow(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_J)
\tag{U4}
\]
uniformly under \textup{(T)}.  For completeness, uniformity follows by the
subsequence criterion: from every sequence satisfying \textup{(T)}, extract
a convergent subsequence of
\(\sqrt N(\sigma_N-\sigma_0)\); boundedness gives Lindeberg, \textup{(U1)}
gives the covariance limit, and the usual even--odd blocking proves the
one-dependent CLT.  The uniform renewal law of large numbers replaces the
deterministic number of pairs by \(K_N-1\), and
\(\widehat\mu_N-\mu_N=o_P(1)\).  These replacements are uniform because the
common exponential moment controls both endpoint cycles and the renewal-count
deviation.  The mean contribution in \textup{(U3)} is
\(O(\sqrt N\,\|m_N\|_{\ell^2})=o(1)\).

The passage from fixed \(J\) to the full statistic is also uniform.  Put
\[
 L_J=\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j\|\phi_j\|_\infty^2\longrightarrow0 .
\]
The even--odd maximal inequality for the centred one-dependent tail feature,
followed by the renewal-count bound \(K_N\le N\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\sigma_N:\,\textup{(T)}}
 \EE_{\sigma_N}\!\left[
 \sum_{j>J}\lambda_jZ_{j,N}^2;\,
 K_N\ge2\right]
 \le C L_J+o(1).
\tag{U5}
\]
Here the \(o(1)\) contains the squared mean from \textup{(U3)} and the event
on which \(\widehat\mu_N\) is outside a fixed compact interval.  The latter
event is exponentially small by the common exponential renewal bound; on its
complement \(\widehat\mu_N\) is uniformly bounded.  This proves
\textup{(U5)} without treating the random number of overlapping pairs as a
conditionally binomial count.

For the limit variable,
\[
 \EE\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j\zeta_j^2
 =\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j\longrightarrow0.
\tag{U6}
\]
Equations \textup{(U4)}--\textup{(U6)} and Markov's inequality give uniform
bounded-Lipschitz convergence of \(Q_N\) to
\(Q_0=\sum_j\lambda_j\zeta_j^2\).  The law of \(Q_0\) is continuous because
\(\lambda_1>0\), so evaluation at \(c_{\alpha,\lambda}\) proves
\textup{(U)}.  Finally,
\[
 (p_N+s_N,p_Ns_N)
 =(2z,z^2-h^2N^{-1/2}),
\]
so the stated \(N^{-1/4}\) root-splitting sequences satisfy \textup{(T)}.
\end{proof}
